first_impression.reaction: I jumped to the FAQ first, as I always do. Then the intro won me over with "is careful about what is documented and what is only often told". Most culture pages just make the meanings up, so a page that admits which bits are folklore is one I'll keep reading. My fiancee's mum is Filipino, so this is relevant to us.

journey.quote: This guide groups the customs couples most often choose by when they happen, explains who does what, and is careful about what is documented and what is only often told.
journey.reaction: Good. Up front about what's solid and what isn't. That's what I want to see.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller rates the Philippines "Exercise a high degree of caution" overall, with higher levels in parts of Mindanao and the Sulu region.
journey.reaction: Dated and sourced, so I can check it myself. I don't usually see a wedding site put the risk in the takeaways.

journey.quote: None of these have a single agreed source, and families keep them to very different degrees.
journey.reaction: Honest. No pretending there's one official list.

journey.quote: The law itself speaks of witnesses, not sponsors.
journey.reaction: Useful. It separates the legal requirement from the cultural one, and that's the distinction I'd actually need for planning.

journey.quote: It is often told that the veil shows the couple being clothed as one.
journey.reaction: "Often told" comes up a lot in this section. I get why, but no source is named for any of the meanings, so I'll be cross-checking them. It's honest hedging, not a problem.

journey.section: Documents and steps from official sources
journey.quote: Not published: a single official checklist of documents and timelines for Australians marrying in the Philippines.
journey.reaction: I respect that they say nobody publishes it instead of making up a timeline. Still, it's the main thing I'd want, so the gap is noticeable.

journey.section: Documents and steps from official sources
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements with you in writing.
journey.reaction: In writing is good, it's something I could hold them to. But at what cost? It doesn't say whether that's part of a paid package or free before I sign.

journey.quote: A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of marriage, but may not work as proof of a name change, so check with your state registry before changing passports or bank details.
journey.reaction: This is the sort of trap I'd fall into. A practical, specific warning.

journey.quote: One person works with you in your time zone, from first idea to the last dance.
journey.reaction: "From first idea to the last dance" is a slogan, not a fact. One person, fine, but what does their fee buy and do they take a cut from the venue? This is the first spot where the page sounds like an ad.

journey.quote: The page was updated on 24 September 2026 and was still current on 2 November 2026.
journey.reaction: Two dates, so I know how fresh this is. Exactly what I want.

journey.quote: There is no single rule. It depends on the families, and many couples now cover much of the cost themselves.
journey.reaction: A fair answer. A typical budget range would have been nice, but I'd rather that than a made-up figure.

unanswered_questions: What does a Wedded Advisor cost, and what does the fee cover? (Deferred to business details, so I'm not expecting it in this article.)
Do you take commission or mark-ups from venues or suppliers you recommend?
Roughly how many months ahead should we start the Philippines paperwork? The page says 'well before invitations go out' but gives no number.
Is there a real Filipino wedding with the actual budget I can look at? The Tuscany link is a story, not a budget.

turn_offs_found.quote: One person works with you in your time zone, from first idea to the last dance.
turn_offs_found.why: A promise with no detail of what's included or what it costs. Mild, because it comes after the evidence, not before it.

would_share_with: My fiancee and her mum, to check which customs their family keeps

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk dates, families and paperwork, your Wedded Advisor is one conversation away.
cta_reaction.why: The content earned enough trust that I'd look at the Concierge page. I won't enquire until I see a fee model and a clear answer on supplier commissions, and that belongs on the business page, not here.

top_3_changes: Swap the slogan 'from first idea to the last dance' in the legal-section CTA for something concrete, e.g. what the Advisor actually does with the paperwork (the 'confirms in writing' line is the better hook).
Give a rough lead time for the Philippines paperwork once it's verified, even as a range with a source, because 'well before invitations go out' won't help me plan.
Where you can, name a source for at least one rite meaning (arras, veil or cord) so the 'often told' hedging doesn't read as hand-waving.
